blockers.description: The three compound sorry cases (imp, and, or) in truthLemma each require a SATURATION structural lemma: if intExpandBranches ... = .openBranch b, then b satisfies semantic closure conditions. Specifically: T(φ∧ψ)@w ∈ b → T(φ)@w ∈ b ∧ T(ψ)@w ∈ b (and analogues for or, imp). This is equivalent to proving that b satisfies intStepBranch b e nw = none for some accumulated expanded set e and next-world nw, AND that every formula in e has its children on b.
blockers.root_cause: When intExpandBranches returns .openBranch bPers, it is because intStepBranch bPers e nw = none for the CURRENT accumulated e and nw (not [] and 0). The expanded set e tracks which formulas have already been expanded; their children were added to bPers. A structural lemma intExpandBranches_openBranch_saturated must be proved by induction on the go inner loop, showing that every compound formula in bPers either (a) is in e with its children in bPers, or (b) returns notApplicable from intApplyRuleFull.
two_options: Option A (structural induction): Prove intExpandBranches_openBranch_saturated by induction on fuel, mirroring the existing intExpandBranches_openBranch_closed proof (which is ~100 lines). This is the preferred approach if the fuel=0 base case can be discharged — however, at fuel=0 the loop picks the first open branch WITHOUT calling intStepBranch, so intStepBranch bPers e nw = none may be FALSE. This makes the fuel=0 base case potentially unprovable without a fuel-sufficiency argument.

Option B (fuel sufficiency): Prove that fuel = 2^(2*φ.complexity+2) is always sufficient to fully saturate the branch before running out of fuel. This allows the fuel=0 case to be vacuously avoided (the algorithm always terminates at fuel>0 with a genuinely saturated branch). Requires a complexity/termination argument showing that the number of distinct expansion steps is bounded by 2^(2*φ.complexity+2).
blockers.recommendation: Option B is more principled but requires a non-trivial combinatorial bound. Option A may be sufficient if we can show the fuel=0 path is never taken in practice (e.g., by modifying the fuel=0 case to return .closed instead of .openBranch, or by separately tracking whether the algorithm terminated normally). Recommend research task to choose and implement the approach.
